This first appeal has been filed by the appellant-wife under Section 19 of the Family Courts Act, 1984 assailing the judgment and decree dated 02.11.2018 passed by the Second Additional Principal Judge, Family Court, Bhopal in R.C.S. No.566-A/2013 (Raju Raikwar vs Smt. Rajkumari Raikwar)
whereby an application preferred by the plaintiff-husband under Section 13(1) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 has been allowed and a decree of divorce has been granted in his favour.
2.

sentences.text: It is the case of the appellant that marriage between the appellant and the respondent was solemnized on 05.07.2006 at Gwalior as per Hindu rites and rituals.

As per the plaint allegations,
the wife has gone to Bhopal and resided along with her brother and Bhabhi.
Both (the appellant and respondent) were in Government service.
The wife used to misbehave and ill-treat the plaintiff and his family members.
An attempt was made to destroy the image of the plaintiff.
A girl child was born out of the wedlock but she was not taken care of by the wife.

On 18.10.2012, the wife had deserted the plaintiff forever and therefore, a divorce petition under Section 13(1) of the Hindu Marriage Act was filed by the respondent-husband before the Family Court, Bhopal on 20.06.2013 praying for dissolution of marriage on the ground of cruelty.
3. On notice being issued, a written submission was filed by the wife denying the plaint allegations.
It is contended therein that from the very beginning, she has been ill-treated, harassed and beaten by the husband and his family members for one or the other reason.
Even at the time of first pregnancy, the wife had to get it aborted due to compelling circumstances created by her in-laws.
After the second pregnancy, when she gave birth to a girl child, she was mentally harassed and tortured as she delivered a girl child.
There was regular demand of dowry and harassment by the respondent and his family members.
Several complaints were lodged including a complaint under Sections 498A and 294 of the IPC against the respondent.
By making all such contentions, she prayed for dismissal of the application filed by the respondent-husband for dissolution of marriage on the ground of cruelty.

4. Before the learned Family Court, the husband got himself examined as PW1 and his younger brother Komal Prasad Raikwar as PW2 whereas the wife got examined herself as DW1 and her father Ram Prasad as DW2.
Several documents have been filed which are exhibited as Ex.P-1 to Ex.P-10.

The learned Family Court after appreciating the oral as well as documentary evidence placed before it, has finally arrived at a conclusion that there is sufficient evidence on record to show desertion by the wife and irretrievable breakdown of marriage and has granted a decree of divorce Smt. sentences.text: vide impugned judgment and decree.
The ground of cruelty which has been raised was turned down by the learned Family Court.
Being aggrieved, present appeal has been preferred by the wife.
Along with this appeal, an application under Order 41 Rule 27 of the CPC has been filed for producing additional documents on record.

5. The main ground of challenge to the impugned judgment and decree is that there was no prayer made in the application under Section 13(1) of the Hindu Marriage Act for dissolution of marriage on the ground of desertion and irretrievable breakdown of marriage.
The divorce petition was filed only on the ground of cruelty.
The factum of cruelty was not found proved by the learned Family Court.
The Family Court has committed a grave error in exceeding its jurisdiction, therefore, the impugned judgment and decree is unsustainable.
There is a specific finding recorded by the Family Court that the ground of cruelty has not been proved against the wife.
It is argued that the marriage cannot be dissolved on the ground of irretrievable breakdown of marriage as being not one of the grounds enumerated under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.
Written statement which has been submitted by the wife and the evidence led by her have not been taken into consideration properly by the Family Court.

The appellant-wife has made an attempt to meet the girl child before the Family Court which was allowed but despite that, the husband and his family members had not permitted her to meet the child on which she has also filed a contempt petition alleging non-compliance of the direction issued by the Family Court.

The ground of adultery which has been raised was also turned down by the Family Court but only on the fact that the parties are residing separately since long which amounts to irretrievable breakdown of marriage, therefore, a decree of divorce was granted to the husband.

6. The respondent-husband has also filed cross-objection by way of Document No.589 of 2019 on 21.01.2019 praying for decree of divorce on the ground of cruelty also pointing out the fact that there are ample evidence available on record with respect to cruelty by the wife which has not been properly appreciated by the Family Court.
It is further contended that the findings given by the Family Court in paras 21 to 38 of the impugned judgment are incorrect as the same is contrary to the evidence on record.

Therefore, he has prayed for setting aside of the part of the judgment whereby it was held that no cruelty as alleged by the respondent-husband for the meaning and purpose of Section 13(1)(i- a) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 could be proved in evidence.

Therefore, prayer is made to reverse the finding regarding issue no.1 in view of attending facts and circumstances of the case.
7.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
8. From the record, it is seen that the marriage between the appellant and the respondent was solemnized on 05.07.2006 at Gwalior as per Hindu rites and rituals.
A girl child was born out of the wedlock coupled with the fact that the wife was residing separately from the husband since 18.10.2012.
It is seen from the record that a complaint (Ex.P/2) was filed by the husband on 21.12.2021 to the Station House Officer, Police Station Aishbag.

sentences.text: She did not used to take care of the girl child who was only three-month old.
She used to ill-treat the family members of the husband.
She herself is an educated woman and purchased a flat at Shivlok colony, Khajuri Kalan, Bhopal.
The aforesaid complaint further finds support from the statement of the husband as well as that of the wife.
She herself admitted in her statement that she is working as Assistant Grade II in Bhopal since 2003 and admitted the fact of Rs.25,000/- being a monthly salary.
She further admitted the fact of purchase of a flat at Shivlok Phase-3 and has been residing there.
There is virtually no counter by the wife to the aforesaid facts.
Even the allegation that she has left her two-year-old girl child and has never bothered to take her care is not disputed by the wife.
On the contrary, she has admitted this fact in her statement coupled with the fact that the girl child was residing with his father and is being taken care of by him.
There is no document on record that she had ever attempted to meet the girl child or take her custody.

The only ground which has been raised by the appellant is with respect to maintainability of the application under Section 13(1) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 seeking divorce within two years from the date of desertion which is against the provisions as mandated in the Hindu Marriage Act and the second ground being the factum of cruelty not found proved and there is no ground with respect to divorce on the ground of irretrievable breakdown of marriage.
Hence, the learned Family Court has exceeded its jurisdiction in granting decree of divorce.

9. As far as the claim of the appellant qua maintainability of the application under Section 13(1) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 seeking divorce within two years from the date of desertion is concerned
, the record indicates that the marriage between the parties was solemnized on 05.07.2006.
On 12.07.2007, the appellant had suffered miscarriage due to some abnormalities in her uterus.
The document to the aforesaid effect is filed as Ex.P/1.
On 02.04.2011, a girl child named Anshika was born.
The evidence on record reflects that there were instances of misbehaving and fight between the parties.

On 21.12.2011, a report was lodged at Police Station Aishbag and Mahila Thana which are marked as Ex.P/2 to the effect that appellant-wife tried to strangulate their eight-months' old daughter and attempted to kill her.
The husband somehow managed to save her.
The appellant misbehaved with the respondent and also beaten him with shoes.
The counselling took place at Police Station Mahila Thana on 24.12.2011 and thereafter, they were required to sign the compromise but the appellant refused to sign.

The respondent again lodged a report at Police Station Mahila Thana vide Ex.P/3 to the effect that father of the appellant threatened him to either give extortion money of Rs.2 Lakhs or the respondent and his family members would be falsely implicated into some dowry case.

On 26.05.2012, a complaint was made to Police Station Aishbag that the appellant-wife had left her matrimonial home and she is threatening for the false implication of the respondent and his family members.
On 18.10.2012, she came back but again left her matrimonial home to live separately in the flat purchased by her.
On 31.10.2012, the appellant came back and stayed in her matrimonial home for four days and again left on 05.11.2012.
On 12.12.2012, the appellant came back and stayed in her matrimonial home for two days and again left on 14.12.2012.

On 30.03.2013, vide Ex.P/6, a report was lodged by the respondent at Police Station Aishbag to the effect that the appellant came on 29.03.2013 to take her belongings and again left her matrimonial home by threatening for the false implication of the respondent and her in- laws.
Thereafter, on 30.04.2013, a false report was got registered under Sections 498A and 294 of the IPC vide Crime No.70/2013 at Police Station Mahila Thana.

sentences.text: The respondent again lodged a report at Police Station Aishbag regarding an attempt being made by the wife to snatch their minor daughter and also the instances of beating the husband.
From the aforesaid narration, dates and events, it is apparently clear that the wife was virtually residing separately since very long.
It is not in dispute that the wife is in Government service and is earning to the tune of Rs.25,000/- per month.
10. The entire evidence available on record shows that the application being filed under Section 13(1) of the Hindu Marriage Act is made out in the attending facts and circumstances of the case.
Therefore, it cannot be said that the application filed by the respondent for dissolution of marriage is not maintainable.
The learned Family Court has dissolved the marriage on the ground of irretrievable breakdown.
Admittedly, the appellant and the respondent are not residing together since long.
There are series of complaints made against each other.

The criminal case registered against respondent for the offence under Sections 498A and 294 of the IPC has resulted into acquittal vide judgment dated 05.11.2018 passed by the Judicial Magistrate First Class, Bhopal in Criminal Case No.3446 of 2013.
11. The question of irretrievable breakdown of marriage was considered by the learned Family Court and a decree of divorce was passed.
From a perusal of the record and statements of the witnesses, it is seen that the averments made in paras 10, 13, 16 and 18 of the application seeking divorce had remained unrebutted.
Statement of PW1 recorded in paras 17 and 24 to 26 showed that they are living separately since long.
As per statement of wife recorded as DW1 in paras 20, 21 and 31 of her deposition, she admitted that she has never tried to contact the respondent or her minor daughter.
No attempt was made by the wife even to take her custody.
She was unaware of the school in which her minor daughter was studying.
Thus, it is apparently clear that the appellant and the respondent are living separately since long.

12. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Ashok Hurra vs Rupa Hurra, AIR 1997 SC 1266 has considered the scope of Article 142 of the Constitution as also the report of the Law Commission on irretrievable breakdown of marriage and held it to be a good ground for dissolving the marriage by granting a decree of divorce.

entities.text: Ashok Hurra vs Rupa Hurra, AIR 1997 SC 1266
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was considered that the proof of such a breakdown would be that the husband and wife have separated and have been living apart, say for a period of five or ten years and it has become impossible to resurrect the marriage or to reunite the parties.

It was stated that once it is known that there are no prospects of the success of the marriage, to drag the legal tie acts as a cruelty to the spouse and gives rise to crime and even abuse of religion to obtain annulment of marriage.

There is no straight jacket formula to consider the definition of 'irretrievable breakdown of marriage'.
13.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Naveen Kohli vs Neelu Kohli, AIR 2006 SC 1675 has considered the aspect of irretrievable breakdown of marriage and held that the same can be made a ground for divorce.

question of irretrievably breakdown of marriage was taken note of by the Hon'ble Supreme Court.

Thus, the learned Family Court has not committed any error in arriving at a conclusion that the appellant and the wife was residing separately since long and considering overall facts and Smt. entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The ground of divorce on the basis of irretrievable breakdown of marriage is made out.
Therefore, the impugned judgment and decree is upheld.
14. So far as the factum of cruelty not found proved by the learned Family Court is concerned, the statement of witnesses have been read over to this Court during the hearing.

The husband has narrated the instances regarding lodging of the report on various occasions against the wife regarding her ill-treatment towards him and his family members as also regarding threatening to get them involved in a false case of demand of dowry.

One such case is registered as Crime No.70 of 2013 at Police Station Mahila Thana for the offence under Sections 498A and 294 of the IPC wherein after trial, the husband has been acquitted vide judgment dated 05.11.2018 passed by Judicial Magistrate First Class, Bhopal in Criminal Case No.3446 of 2013.
The appellant has made the life of the respondent miserable like hell.
She further admitted that she does not want to reside with the respondent-husband in her deposition recorded by the learned Family Court.
Their marriage has been wrecked beyond hope of salvage and looking to the factum of dispute between the husband and wife, there is no possibility of reconciliation.
The act of the wife amounts to cruelty including mental cruelty to her husband and his family members.
However, the same has not been defined but the same can always be borne out from the instances that took place during the marriage period.
15. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Samar Ghosh vs Jaya Ghosh, (2007) 4 SCC 511 has considered the instances of cruelty and irretrievable breakdown as ground of divorce.

entities.text: Samar Ghosh vs Jaya Ghosh, (2007) 4 SCC 511
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, in the case of K. Shrinivas Rao vs D.A. Deepa, AIR 2013 SC 2176, ground for divorce on the ground of mental cruelty was considered.

entities.text: K. Shrinivas Rao vs D.A. Deepa, AIR 2013 SC 2176
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the case of Parveen Mehta vs. Inderjit Mehta, (2002) 5 SCC 706,
it has been held :

entities.text: Parveen Mehta vs. Inderjit Mehta, (2002) 5 SCC 706
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "21. Cruelty for the purpose of Section 13(1)(i-a) is to be taken as a behaviour by one spouse towards the other, which causes reasonable apprehension in the mind of the latter that it is not safe for him or her to continue the matrimonial relationship with the other.
Mental cruelty is a state of mind and feeling with one of the spouses due to the behaviour or behavioural pattern by the other.

Unlike the case of physical cruelty,
mental cruelty is difficult to establish by direct evidence.
It is necessarily a matter of inference to be drawn from the facts and circumstances of the case.

A feeling of anguish, disappointment and frustration in one spouse caused by the conduct of the other can only be appreciated on assessing the attending facts and circumstances in which the two partners of matrimonial life have been living.
The inference has to be drawn from the attending facts and circumstances taken cumulatively.

In case of mental cruelty it will not be a correct approach to take an instance of misbehaviour in isolation and then pose the question whether such behaviour is sufficient by itself to cause mental cruelty.

The approach should be to take the cumulative effect of the facts and circumstances emerging from the evidence on record and then draw a fair inference whether the petitioner in the divorce petition has been subjected to mental cruelty due to conduct of the other."

In A. Jayachandra vs Aneel Kaur, (2005) 2 SCC 22, the Hon'ble Supreme Court observed as under:
"10.

entities.text: A. Jayachandra vs Aneel Kaur, (2005) 2 SCC 22
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The expression 'cruelty'
has not been defined in the Act.
Cruelty can be physical or mental.

Cruelty which is a ground for dissolution of marriage may be defined as wilful and unjustifiable conduct of such character as to cause danger to life, limb or health, bodily or mental, or as to give rise to a reasonable apprehension of such a danger.

The question of mental cruelty has to be considered in the light of the norms of marital ties of the particular society to which the parties belong, their social values,
status, environment in which they live.
Cruelty, as noted above, includes mental cruelty, which falls within the purview of a matrimonial wrong.
Cruelty need not be physical.

If from the conduct of the spouse same is established and/or an inference can be legitimately drawn that the treatment of the spouse is such that it causes an apprehension in the mind of the other spouse, about his or her mental welfare then this conduct amounts to cruelty.

In a delicate human relationship like matrimony,
one has to see the probabilities of the case.

The concept, proof beyond the shadow of doubt, is to be applied to criminal trials and not to civil matters and certainly not to matters of such delicate personal relationship as those of husband and wife.

Therefore, one has to see what are the probabilities in a case and legal cruelty has to be found out, not merely as a matter of fact, but as the effect on the mind of the complainant spouse because of the acts or omissions of the other.
Cruelty may be physical or corporeal or may be mental.
In physical cruelty, there can be tangible and direct evidence, but in the case of mental cruelty there may not at the same time be direct evidence.
In cases where there is no direct evidence, courts are required to probe into the mental process and mental effect of incidents that are brought out in evidence.
It is in this view that one has to consider the evidence in matrimonial disputes."

17. In Vinita Saxena vs Pankaj Pandit, (2006) 3 SCC 778, the Hon'ble Apex Court observed thus :
"37.

entities.text: Vinita Saxena vs Pankaj Pandit, (2006) 3 SCC 778
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As to what constitutes the required mental cruelty for the purposes of the said provision, will not depend upon the numerical count of such incidents or only on the continuous course of such conduct but really go by the intensity, gravity and stigmatic impact of it when meted out even once and the deleterious effect of it on the mental attitude, necessary for maintaining a conducive matrimonial home.

38. If the taunts, complaints and reproaches are of ordinary nature only, the court perhaps need consider the further question as to whether their continuance or persistence over a period of time render, what normally would, otherwise, not be so serious an act to be so injurious and painful as to make the spouse charged with them genuinely and reasonably conclude that the maintenance of matrimonial home is not possible any longer."

entities.text: Rajkuimari Raikwar W/O Raju ... vs Raju Raikwar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: All these judgments were considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Samar Ghosh's case (supra).

From the aforesaid judgment as well as after appreciating the evidence available on record,
it is apparently clear that the factum of cruelty by the wife against the respondent stands proved.
Therefore, the finding recorded by the learned Family Court regarding cruelty not being proved is unsustainable.
The cross-objection has already been filed by the respondent as far as the finding recorded by the learned Family Court with respect to factum of cruelty.

Under these circumstances,
aforesaid part of the impugned judgment as it finds mention in para 38 thereof, is set aside.

19. Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case and the factum of cruelty being proved, the learned Family Court ought to have granted a decree of divorce on the ground of cruelty as there is no possibility to reconcile the marriage between the parties especially taking note of the fact that the wife in her deposition herself refused to reside with the husband and no attempt was made by her even to take custody of the girl child at any point of time.
20. In the result, the appeal filed by the appellant-wife is dismissed.
So far as the cross objection filed by the respondent-husband is concerned
, the same is allowed.
The part of the impugned judgment whereby it has been held that allegation of cruelty is not found proved is hereby set aside.
The marriage solemnized between the parties on 05.07.2006 is declared to be dissolved on the ground of cruelty as well as on irretrievable breakdown of marriage.
21. Registry is directed to draw a decree in accordance with the aforesaid observations.
